task.description: WF-03 Step 1b: independently validate CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0429-async-alert-hook-delivery.md against ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis and the real source (application.ex, alerts.ex, poller.ex) -- no implementation code, full acceptance-relevant coverage, ordering-hazard claim verified against actual application.ex/poller.ex text, crash-observability mechanics of Task.Supervisor.start_child/2 verified, check_and_record_emission/4 ordering re-derived from source, ambiguity check, test-approach soundness, moduledoc-drift action item confirmed explicit.

result.summary: PASS on all six checks. (1) No literal implementation code: only two fenced blocks in the doc (lines 174-184, 187-207) and both are ASCII before/after sequence diagrams, not Elixir syntax; every backtick reference elsewhere is a short function/module/spec name or an inline type-signature description, not a code body -- consistent with this run's prior rework fixes (290c6b2/3680243). (2) Application.ex read in full: children list matches the design's description exactly -- the six existing Task.Supervisors, then `] ++ scheduler_children() ++ http_child()`, with scheduler_children/0 gated on `:start_scheduler` and its own comment independently confirming 'the Poller's own first tick runs with ZERO delay.' poller.ex's init/1 confirms this directly: `Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0)`. The ordering hazard is real: placing the new Task.Supervisor after scheduler_children() would let the zero-delay first tick attempt `Task.Supervisor.start_child(Letflow.Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor, ...)` before that name is registered. Mechanistically this is a GenServer.call to an unregistered name, which raises an :exit (Kernel.exit/1 inside the caller), NOT a rescuable exception and NOT caught by poller.ex's `try/rescue` (rescue clauses do not catch :exit) -- it would crash the Poller's handle_info clause outright, not merely return an {:error, :noproc} tuple. The design's own text hedges between these two outcomes ('return {:error, :noproc} (or fail with a noproc exit if not handled)') rather than stating the precise mechanism, but this is a rationale-precision nit, not a correctness or ambiguity defect: the design's actual instruction (place the new supervisor before scheduler_children(), no ordering constraint relative to the other six) is unambiguous and correct regardless of which failure mode is named, and no code needs to handle the wrong-order case since the design does not choose that order. Not required as a rework item. (3) fire_hooks/4, check_and_record_emission/4, and deliver_with_retry/4 read in full at lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:405-520: matches the design's description exactly -- check_and_record_emission/4 runs synchronously and commits (on_conflict: :replace_all, conflict_target: [:hook_id, :trigger_key]) unconditionally before deliver_with_retry/4 is ever invoked, and this commit does not depend on delivery's own side effects in any way (the emission row's only inputs are hook_id/trigger_key/emitted_key, all known before dispatch) -- confirms relocating only deliver_with_retry/4 cannot introduce a new dedupe race; two ticks passing the dedupe check before either completes delivery is impossible because the dedupe check IS the synchronous DB write, not a read of a delivery-derived value. (4) Ambiguity check: Task.Supervisor child spec, restart policy (default :temporary, no :max_children/:max_restarts/:max_seconds override), naming, comment-convention contents, and dispatch mechanism (start_child/2, not async_nolink/2) are all stated as explicit decisions with stated reasons, not left to ELIXIR-DEV's discretion. (5) Crash-observability mechanics (the design's most safety-critical claim) verified independently and confirmed CORRECT: Task.Supervisor.start_child/2 tasks use proc_lib under the hood; on an unhandled raise/exit, proc_lib's own crash-report path (independent of whether anything is watching the result) logs the crash via the standard :logger/SASL crash-report mechanism -- this is also Elixir's own documented behavior for Task.Supervisor.start_child/2 ('If the task fails, an error is logged, but the process that started the task will not be notified'). No async_nolink/handle_info correlation is needed for observability; the design correctly distinguishes this from ISS-0224's actual original hazard (synchronous execution inside a GenServer callback), which this fix also does not reintroduce, since start_child/2 returns immediately just as async_nolink/2 would. (6) poller.ex's maybe_run_alert_detection/3 (lines 148-160) read in full and matches the design's characterization exactly: try/rescue wraps only Alerts.build_context_and_detect/3, rescue clause is `_ -> :ok`, unaffected by relocating deliver_with_retry/4 since that call graph will return before any dispatched task's own crash can occur. (7) Test approach (design section 6) is precise and consistent with source: poller.ex's start_link/1 does hardcode `name: __MODULE__` (confirmed by direct read), and the design correctly derives from this that the test must run `async: false`; on_exit cleanup, sandbox-mode handling, and the fail-first requirement (WF-03 Step 4) are all specified. (8) Moduledoc-drift item (alerts.ex lines 38-42 'No new periodic process' / lines 65-69 'OQ-4 resolution') is stated in design section 7 as an explicit action item for ELIXIR-DEV to update, not left implicit -- line numbers verified exact via grep against the live file. (9) webhooks.ex out-of-scope claim independently re-verified: `grep -rn 'Webhooks.deliver(' lib/` outside webhooks.ex itself returns no matches, confirming it is currently latent as the design and ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis both state. VERDICT: PASS. Routing to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation.
